TH Khan, Senior Advocate with AB Mahmudul Haque, Advocate—for the Appellant. 
Dr Rafiqur Rahman, Senior Advocate with Md Ismail, Advocate—For the Respondent.
parties:
A.K. Khan and Co. Ltd. ------ Petitioner
vs
Zanak Enterprise ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
A.B.M. Khairul Haque, J: This first miscellaneous appeal arises out of the judgment and order dated 26-1-1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 158 of 1994, allowing the miscellaneous case filed under Order XXI rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The facts leading to the filing of this first miscellaneous appeal are that one Zanak Enterprise, the respondent, in response to a notice, published on 26-2-1989, purchased a trawler in an open auction from Bangladesh Fisheries Development Corporation (BFDC) at a price of Taka 3,30,000/- and also obtained possession of the same but suddenly on 17-8-1989, the police seized the said vessel, that on enquiry from the Court, they could learn that a criminal case had been filed by the decree-holder. Thereafter, they filed an application in the Money Execution Case No. 79 of 1984 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Chittagong, under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code on 19-8-1984. Initially, this was treated as an application, subsequently, since 8-9-1994; this was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 158 of 1994. In the said miscellaneous case Ms AK Khan and Co., the decree-holder appellant filed a written objection on 27-9-1994, contending, inter alia, that the trawler in dispute, namely, Taiko Maru No. 5, along with three other trawlers were under attachment since 5-6-1981 firstly, in the Money Suit No. 114 of 1981, in which suit they obtained a decree for Taka 82,84,874.34/- on 19-1-1982 and thereafter in their Money Execution Case No. 79 of 1984. In due course, the said trawler was sold out in open auction and was also delivered in their favour on 17-8-1989. As such, the application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code is not maintainable. 

 3. At the time of hearing of the miscellaneous case, evidence was led both on behalf of the third party petitioner as well as on behalf of the decree-holder purchaser. The learned Judge on consideration of the evidence on record found that the concerned trawler was not attached on 16-3-1989 in the Money Execution Case No. 79 of 1984 filed by the decree-holder and that before such alleged attachment, the petitioner-respondent obtained ownership in the said trawler and that the papers regarding auction and sale were mere paper transaction and was never acted upon. On these findings the learned Judge allowed the miscellaneous case under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code filed by the 3rd party respondent and released the disputed trawler Taiko Maru No. 5 from attachment and auction sale by his Order dated 26-1-1995. Being aggrieved the decree holder first obtained a Rule under section 115 of the Code on 6-6-1995 but subsequently, on the prayer of the petitioner the Rule was converted into first miscellaneous appeal by order of this Court dated 4-6-2001, converting the Civil Revision No. 2044 of 1995 in the present appeal. 

 5. Mr. T. H Khan, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant, assails the order dated 26-1-1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge allowing the miscellaneous case filed under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code mainly on the ground that once in compliance of the provisions of Order XXI, the sale of the property in auction becomes final as it happened in this case, followed by delivery of possession by the jimmadar on 17-8-1989, in compliance of the direction of the Court, the objection raised at a belated stage on 19-8-1989 purportedly under Order XXI, rule 58 has got no manner of application and was misconceived. Besides he submits that even on the showing of the third party in the said miscellaneous case that they purchased the trawler, namely, Taiko Maru No. 5, and not Taiko Maru No. 5, which would be evident from the execution of the receipt dated 18-3-1989 (Ext. 1) by their seller, Bangladesh Fisheries Development Corporation, as such, their purchased trawler being a different one, they could not have any interest in the trawler, namely, Taiko Maru No. 5. 

 6. On the other hand, Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the third party respondent, submits that they on good faith purchased the concerned trawler from a Government statutory corporation, being Bangladesh Fisheries Development Corporation, being the highest bidder in an open tender at a consideration of Taka 3.30,000/- and thereafter, also incurred huge expenditure in salvaging the same from underneath the mud and to make it seaworthy. He however concedes that what they purchased initially was the trawler Taiko Maru No. 5 but subsequently, the said name was changed to Taiko Maru No. 5 by the seller themselves, on the contention that earlier the name of the trawler was written mistakenly which was a mere typographical mistake made in the plaint and since they obtained the ownership and possession they are entitled to maintain this miscellaneous case and the learned Judge rightly found that the trawler Taiko Maru No. 5 was never under attachment by order of any Court. As such, he prays for dismissal of the appeal. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and also perused the relevant papers on record. It appears that the episode in this case started with the filing of the suit on behalf of A.K. Khan & Company Ltd. against M/s Puso and Company and two others being Money Suit No. 114 of 1981, in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Chittagong, on 27-5-1981, praying for a decree for recovery of money and damages for Taka 82, 84,874.34/-. On the next day they also filed an application under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 of the Code, praying for attachment before judgment of the following vessels, namely, (1) Taiko Maru No. 2, (2) Taiko Maru No. 5(3) Trawler Akitso Maru No. 11 and (4) Kyoshine Maru No. 21. Those vessels were in the safe custody of Harbour Master of Chittagong. The Court on hearing the plaintiff petitioner by its order dated 5-6-1981, attached those trawlers lying in the Karnafully River in front of Ralli Ghat at Bangla Bazar, Chittagong and the bailiff of the Court put the said trawlers under the custody of the Harbour Master. In due course, the suit was decreed ex parte on 19-1-1982 against Puso and Company, defendant No. 1, Nonaka Sangyo Company Ltd, defendant No. 2 and Bangla Marine Products Ltd, defendant No. 4. The trawlers which were under attachment, belonged to defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3. The defendant No. 4 was an associate of the defendant No. 2. Thereafter an execution case being Money Execution Case No. 8 of 1983 was filed on 22-6-1983, to execute the decree for Taka 82, 84,874.34/- obtained by the plaintiff appellant against the aforementioned defendant judgment debtors. This execution case was renumbered as Money Execution Case No. 79 of 1984 on being transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Chitttagong. In the said execution case the name of the following trawlers were mentioned, namely, (1) FT Kyeshin Maru No. 21, registration No. 83225 (2) FT Taiko Maru No. 5, registration No. 10971, (3) FT Akitsu Maru No. 11, registration No. 67161. In due course those trawlers mentioned in the petition for execution, was attached under Order XXI, rule 30 on 16-3-1989. Subsequently, notices were published in different news-papers for sale of those trawlers in public auction on 30-4-1989. In due course, the auction of the trawlers. Taiko Maro No. 5 and Akitsu Maru No. 11 was finally held on 30-7-1989 and the decree holder itself purchased the concerned trawlers at a consideration of Taka 17, 65,000/-. Thereafter the decree holder after paying the sale fee, applied for delivery of possession in their favour and the Court by its order dated 15-8-1989 directed the jimmadar of the attached trawler to deliver the possession of those two trawlers in favour of the decree holder auction purchaser. The said order of the Court was communicated to the jimmadar vide memo No. 403 dated 16-8-1989. Accordingly, the jimmadar, one Ferozul Quader Khan, handed over the physical possession of those two trawlers including Taiko Maru No. 5 on 17-8-1989 in favour of one Shawkat Hossain, the representative of the decree-holder and informed the Court by his application dated 20-8-1989. 

 9. At that time, had the learned Second Subordinate Judge, considered the matter closely, he could have found that the alleged inadvertence to mention the name of the trawler Taiho Maru No. 5 instead of Taiko Maru No. 5 was not due to typographical error as alleged in paragraphs 8 and 9 of their petition for amendment of the plaint, rather, the auction purchaser Zanak Enterprise discovered that although the name of the vessel they purchased was Taiho Maru No. 5 but they got another vessel namely, Taiko Maru No. 5 as stated in paragraph 7 of their petition for amendment of the petitions dated 21-6-1983 and dated 6-8-1988, praying for attachment and sale respectively of the vessel Taiho Maru. Perusal of those two applications dated 13-9-1989 for amendment of the name of  the vessel would unmistakably show that the plaintiff BFDC made those two applications for amendment of the name of the vessel not because of their discovery of their alleged mistake in the official records, rather, they did so on the information given to them by the auction purchaser. But they being total strangers to the earlier transitions and business relationship between the BFDC and the defendant, Bangla Marine Products Ltd were not at all in a position to know as to which vessel was left by the defendant at the jetty of the BFDC. Rather, the letters of the BFDC dated 4-3-1989 (Ext. 2ka in Misc. Case No. 158 of 1994) and dated 19-3-1989 (Ext. 2 in Misc. Case No. 158 of 1994) addressed to Zanak Enterprise, would unmistakably show that the vessel Taiho Maru No. 5 was sold in auction to them and not the vessel Taiko Maru No. 5. This will become all the more clear from the receipt dated 18-3-1989 (Ext. 1) given by the BFDC to Zanak Enterprise for an amount of Taka 3, 30,000/- towards the price for the vessel Taiho Maru No. 5. 

 11. It is apparent from the resume of the facts stated above that the concerned trawler was under attachment of the Court since 5-6-1981 firstly, under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 of the Code on the prayer of the plaintiff in Money Suit No. 114 of 1981, thereafter in pursuance of the provisions of Order XXI of the Code in Money Execution Case No. 78 of 1984, the concerned trawler along with other trawlers were attached on 16-3-1989. As such, it is apparent that M/s Zanak Enterprise, the third party respondent, purchased the trawler Taiho Maru No. 5 by money receipt dated 18-3-1989 from the plaintiff of Money Suit No. 1163 of 1984 and not Taiko Maru No. 5. As such, the question of purchasing the said vessel by them does not arise in spite of the illegal amendment of the name by an order dated 23-9-1989. 

 The respondent Zanak Enterprise purchased the vessel Taiho Maru No. 5 and not the vessel Taiko Maru No. 5, as such, it has no claim of ownership on the said vessel and the miscellaneous case filed under Order XXI, rule 58 ought to have been rejected. 

 12. Even if it is assumed that Zanak Enterprise purchased Taiko Maru No. 5 but the said vessel was already under attachment of the Court since 5-6-1981, in MS Suit No. 114 of 1981 and then again was attached in connection with Money Execution Case No. 79 of 1984 on 16-3-1989. Besides, it is also apparent from the records that the physical possession of the trawler Taiko Maru No. 5 had already been handed over in favour of the decree-holder AK Khan and Co on 17-8-1989 by Firojul Kader Khan, the jimmader, in pursuance of the orders of the Court dated 15-8-1989 in the execution proceedings in the Execution Case No. 79 of 1984, filed by AK Khan & Co., the decree-holder petitioner, regarding sale in auction of the concerned trawlers. 

 "From the plain reading of the above provision it is clear that the moment the purchaser pays the purchase money, the sale becomes absolute under sub-rule (2) and no further formal order of the Court is required as in the case of a sale of immovable property under rule 92 of Order XXI. 

 14. In the instant case, AK Khan & Co., the decree-holder obtained a decree for Taka 82,84,874.34/-. Four trawlers including Taiko Maru No. 5 were under attachment firstly, since 5-6-1981 under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 in Money Suit No. 114 of 1981 and thereafter the Court, in Money Execution Case No. 79 of 1984, by its Order dated 9-3-1989, issued an order of attachment which was returned after service on 22-3-1989. In due course, the decree-holder filed an application on 20-7-1989 praying for participation in the auction sale to be held on 30-7-1990 which was allowed by the Court. On that date, on the prayer of the decree-holder, the time of 15 days was allowed to file sale-fee and accordingly, the decree-holder submitted court-fees of Taka 17,750/- towards sale-fees on 14-8-1989 and the auction on its behalf was accepted by the Court on that date. On the next date, on 15-8-1989, on the prayer of the decree -holder, the Court ordered release of the trawler from attachment and directed the jimmader to hand over the auctioned property in favour of the decree-holder-auction purchaser. This Order of the Court was communicated to the jimmader by Memo No. 403 dated 16-8-1989. The jimmader, accordingly, handed over the trawler in favour of the decree-holder-auction-purchaser on 17-8-1989. 

 15. It is palpably clear that in the morning on 17-8-1989 when the trawler namely, Taiko Maru No. 5 was handed over by the jimmadar to the auction purchaser decree holder the whole proceedings came to an end. Even prior to that date, the auction sale of the trawler which is a movable property, as envisaged under the various provisions of Order XXI has reached its finality on 14-8-1989 when the decree holder auction purchaser paid the sale-fees. As such, the contention of Mr TH Khan, the learned Advocate that after finalisation of the sale in auction it cannot be challenged in-a proceeding under Order XXI, rule 58 has got substance. On payment of the sale-fees on 14-8-1989 and after actual delivery of possession of the vessel on 17-8-1989 whole proceedings of the execution, started with the attachment, followed by auction and thereafter sale, reached its finality and cannot be re-opened under any of the provisions of Order XXI not to speak of under rule 58, because Rule 58 envisages an investigation as to the claim of the petitioner, who is a stranger to the suit, during the pendency of attachment made in the execution case and not thereafter when the concerned property had already been released from such attachment. In this case, it is apparent that on 19-8-1989, when the miscellaneous case was filed there was no existence of any attachment; the concerned vessels had already been sold in auction and was physically handed over to the decree-holder-auction-purchaser. In that view of the matter also the miscellaneous case filed under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code, praying for release of the trawler, namely, Taiko Maru No. 5 from attachment was misconceived and was not maintainable and was liable to be rejected. 

 16. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the judgment and order passed in the miscellaneous case is set aside.
